newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-LATIF INTERVIEW REVIVES ROW OVER BETTING.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LATIF INTERVIEW REVIVES ROW OVER BETTING.

text.p: The row over cricket wagering erupted again on Tuesday with Indian players denying reported charges by former Pakistan vice-captain Rashid Latif of unprofessional activities.

Latif, who was Salim Malik's deputy during the 1995 tour of South Africa and Zimbabwe, was quoted as telling India's "Outlook" magazine which was published on Tuesday that four Indian cricketers -- Mohammed Azharuddin, Ajay Jadeja, Venkatapathy Raju and Navjot Sidhu -- would call him to seek information on pitches and teams.

"Azhar bhai (Azharuddin), Jaddu (Jadeja), Raju, Sidhu and some other Indian players used to telephone me at home to find out how the pitch was. Whether it would aid batting or bowling, how strong the teams were and what the weather was like," Latif was quoted as saying in an interview.
"They had to pass on information to other people," Latif said. "I used to oblige generally as it was nothing wrong on my side."
But the Indian cricketers, who are currently in Colombo to play in the Asia Cup competition, denied the charges.
"Whatever things have been written are not true. What I say is these allegations are unconfirmed, they are not right," Azharuddin said.
The former Indian captain said he had received a letter from Latif in which the former Pakistan wicket-keeper had denied speaking to the magazine.
"The fax from Latif is very clear. I hope it will clear everything," he said.
Sidhu said he never knew Latif.

The involvement of cricketers with bookies is currently being probed by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) after former test player Manoj Prabhakar accused an unnamed team mate of offering him a bribe of 2.5 million rupees ($70,000) to perform badly in the 1994 Singer Cup match against Pakistan.
The BCCI has named former Supreme Court chief justice Y.V. Chandrachud to inquire into Prabhakar's allegations of match-fixing against Indian cricketers.
Former Indian managers Ajit Wadekar and Ashok Mankad, former test captain Dilip Vengsarkar and cricketer Sanjay Manjreker appeared before Chandrachud in Bombay on Tuesday.

Details of their testimony were not made public, but the Press Trust of India news agency quoted U.N. Banerjee, the legal adviser to BCCI, as saying: "None of them have been involved in the allegations and we just wanted to know their opinions about such allegations."
